newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bank shares boosted by bonds bounce.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bank shares boosted by bonds bounce.

text.p: Shares in most major banks followed the bond market higher on Wednesday with National Australia Bank Ltd jumping over two percent to an intraday high of A$13.79 and Westpac Banking Corporation adding 12 cents to a record high of A$7.04.
Australia and New Zealand Banking Corporation Ltd added 1.4 percent to an intraday high of A$7.30.
Traders said the rally in bonds, both locally and in the U.S., had provided the impetus for investor's interest in the sector, aided by some switching from resource stocks.

"I think it's on the back of bonds," said Greg Matthews, executive director of Australian equities at Mercantile Mutual, adding that while takeover speculation remained rife in the sector, little fresh information had emerged.
"The ANZ and Standard Chartered one was a new one but there is still plenty going on in terms of Wallis (inquiry)," Matthews said.

ANZ Bank and U.K.-based Standard Chartered Plc were reported on October 28 as considering a merger, although the report was denied by ANZ Bank and Standard Chartered said it did not comment on market rumours.
London banking analysts dismissed the speculation describing it as another pointless takeover rumour.

Local brokers agreed that while bonds had led the banks higher today, the same old takeover speculation was underpinning the share price of some of the major banks and pointed to the choppy trading seen by Commonwealth Bank of Australia, which firmed early but was softer in the afternoon session despite a stronger overall sector.
"If anything, there is more takeover speculation in the other banks but it's the same old story. I don't think you can read too much into it," said a Sydney broker.
The two most popular rumours circulating about the major banks this year had National Australia Bank buying Westpac and banking giant HSBC Holdings Plc as bidding for ANZ Bank.

ANZ Bank shares closed 10 cents higher at A$7.30, National Australia Bank shares closed 28 cents higher at A$13.75, Westpac shares closed 11 cents up at A$7.03 while Commonwealth Bank shares closed three cents lower at A$11.84.
